Ciechanow New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ciechanów, Poland

Demolished. This third, newer Ciechanów cemetery (see the Ciechanów Old Jewish Cemetery record for the town's fuller community history) was purchased in 1873 in the Aleksandrówka neighborhood, later expanded south to about 2.25 hectares; first burials likely occurred in the 1880s, with regular funerals continuing until November 1942. During WWII, it also served as an execution and mass-burial site, including non-Jewish bodies exhumed and reinterred in 1945. Germans devastated the cemetery in 1942, dismantling the fence and removing tombstones - only rows of trees now mark the historic boundaries. In 1947, survivors formed a Jewish Religious Association to clean the site, placing symbolic stepped-pyramid monuments (built from recovered matzevot) at Sara Altus's exhumed grave and the northern corner; a caretaker agreement lasted from 1949 until the 1980s. In 1962, the Ciechanów Landsmanshaft in Paris rebuilt the monument as a fenced mausoleum reading 'Here, the ashes of Jews murdered by the Nazi occupiers in Ciechanów rest. Honor their memory!' Ground-penetrating radar research in 2015-2016 confirmed the location of the 1942 mass grave and clarified the cemetery's boundaries.
